sourceIssues.locator: BSTTTZ, arXiv:1701.02458v1, §7, Remark 7.2, printed p.10, the displayed class number formula (checked on a page image); the corresponding place in the February 2017 author copy was not checked
sourceIssues.reason: Write zeta_C(s) = Z(|k|^(-s)) with Z(T) = P(T)/((1-T)(1-|k|T)) and P(1) = |Pic^0(C)(k)|. The pole at s = 1 comes from the factor 1 - |k|T, and the residue is P(|k|^(-1))/((1 - |k|^(-1)) log|k|); the functional equation P(1/(|k|T)) = |k|^(-g) T^(-2g) P(T) at T = 1 gives P(|k|^(-1)) = |k|^(-g) P(1). Hence P(1) = |k|^g (1 - |k|^(-1)) log|k| Res, and the printed identity omits 1 - |k|^(-1). That factor lies in [1/2, 1), so the remark, which only compares growth in g, is unaffected.

sourceIssues.locator: BSTTTZ, arXiv:1701.02458v1, §7, Remark 7.3, printed p.10 (checked on a page image); the corresponding place in the February 2017 author copy was not checked
sourceIssues.printed: Pic^0(C)(k)[2] subset Pic^0(C)(kbar)[2] and the latter group has size 2^(2g), or 2^g if the characteristic is 2
sourceIssues.correction: ... or at most 2^g if the characteristic is 2.
sourceIssues.reason: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 2 the 2-torsion of a g-dimensional abelian variety is (Z/2)^f with f the 2-rank, 0 <= f <= g; f = g characterises the ordinary case and a supersingular Jacobian has f = 0. Only the upper bound is used: the remark compares |k|^g with 2^(2g) in odd characteristic and with 2^g in characteristic 2, and concludes that the first bound of Theorem 7.1 wins only for k = F_3. That conclusion is unaffected, and is correct with the corrected statement.

sourceIssues.locator: Author copy §4, first paragraph, p.6 (index-two case of the proof of Theorem 1.1)
sourceIssues.printed: by genus theory, the 2-torsion in the class group of K is bounded by the 2-torsion in the class group of F multiplied by O(2^t) … we obtain a bound of O_ε(|Disc(K)|^{1/4+ε})
sourceIssues.correction: Use the relative bound that is proved, h_2(K) ≤ 4^{e−1} h_2(F)² (Klüners–Wang, arXiv:2003.12161, Theorem 2.1, with e counting ramified places including real ones). With Theorem 1.1 for F (or Gauss genus theory when F is quadratic) and D_F ≤ D_K^{1/2}, this gives h_2(K) ≪ D_K^{1/2−1/(2n)+ε} for n > 4 and D_K^ε when n = 4, so Theorem 1.1 is unaffected; the D_K^{1/4+ε} bound for this case is not established.
sourceIssues.reason: The one-factor bound is asserted without proof or reference. The published relative genus bounds (Cornell; Klüners–Wang) carry the square of h_2(F); the linear form is proved there only when the base 2-rank is zero. The checkpoint already routes the Klüners–Wang replacement (quadratic-relative-rank, quadratic-relative-torsion).

sourceIssues.locator: Author copy Theorem 1.3 and the paragraph before it, pp.2–3; same statement in arXiv v1
sourceIssues.printed: |Sel_2(Jac(C))| = O_ε(|Disc(K)|^ε h_2(K)); (a) |Sel_2(Jac(C))| = O_ε(|Disc(K)|^{1/2−δ_n+ε}); (b) rank(Jac(C)) < c_ε + (1/2−δ_n+ε) log_2|Disc(K)|
sourceIssues.correction: The ε-factor must be |Disc(C)|^ε: |Sel_2(Jac C)| ≪_{n,ε} |Disc(C)|^ε h_2(K) ≪ |Disc(C)|^ε |Disc(K)|^{1/2−δ_n+ε}. Theorem 1.3 holds in the Disc(C) form that the remark after Theorem 1.3 allows.
sourceIssues.reason: K = Q[x]/(f) does not see the twists of C. Take f(x) = x³ − N²x: then K ≅ Q³, so Disc(K) = 1 and h_2(K) = 1, and (a) would bound |Sel_2| uniformly over the congruent-number curves y² = x³ − N²x. Their 2-Selmer ranks are unbounded (Heath-Brown 1993–94; Swinnerton-Dyer 2008; Kane 2013). Part (b) is deduced from (a), so it is not established with Disc(K); with Disc(C) both parts follow.
